content:
Tech journalist Kara Swisher on Tuesday unloaded on Scott Jennings, using her recent exit from CNN to reveal her true feelings about the network’s “boneheaded” conservative heel, who has regularly defended President Donald Trump and his offensive antics on the air.

A former CNN contributor herself, Swisher blasted the MAGA pundit in a viral Threads post.

“Now that I am out [of] my CNN gig, I can more flatly say what I do not miss [is] the always knuckleheaded but persistently willful compromises of Scott Jennings, who never had a boneheaded take he did not express with the smugness of Tracy Flick,” she wrote Tuesday.

Tracy Flick, of course, is a fictional character played by Reese Witherspoon in the 1999 film “Election.” The adaptation was widely lauded by critics, as Witherspoon expertly portrayed Flick’s central traits — namely ruthless ambition, entitlement and insecurity.

Swisher was reacting to a recent blunder from Jennings, who told “NewsNight” guest host Elie Honig on Monday to “lighten up a little and chuckle” about Trump’s latest social media antic.

The president had posted an AI-generated meme depicting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with blood on his face, hoisting a bra and pumping his fist, in a play on the famous photo of Trump after his attempted assassination in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024.

While Huang resigned earlier this month amid reports of several extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy, Trump posted the image in celebration of Huang being reinstated. Jennings staunchly defended the decision Monday — which Swisher couldn’t help but mock.

“Haha a bra is the level of discourse for maladjusted teens, not a grown-ass man,” she wrote.

Trump owns up to $62 million worth of Nvidia shares — and openly admitted Monday that he was instrumental in having Huang reinstated as CEO.

Jennings echoed Trump in dismissing national security concerns about Huang’s return, stating, “I’m team America.”

He also staunchly defended the AI image itself when Honig asked what was funny about it.

Jennings said, “Do you really need me to spell it out for you? I mean, you could just lighten up a little and chuckle. I mean, it’s a meme.” Honig ultimately noted that it probably wasn’t funny to the family of Corey Comperatore, a rallygoer who died at the Butler shooting.

Jennings doubled down, of course, and said the family is “very grateful” to Trump.

Swisher appears ecstatic about leaving CNN, whose parent company, Warner Bros. Discovery, has been acquired by Paramount Skydance and its Trump ally CEO David Ellison. Her contract is set to expire at the end of this year, and Swisher initially considered staying.
